evidence.description: Reviewed all 18 declared/live slots; confirmed no 'risk' field exists anywhere yet (expected pre-implementation, but the REQ-201 default-value and always-available-slot mechanisms needed to populate it are underspecified, see FIND-001/FIND-002).
Confirmed the cited line ranges for the registry read (~L104-118) and fetchUsdcBalance call (~L192) are accurate and structurally coherent with a per-wake filter call between them.
Verified all cross-references cited in behavioral-spec.md's intro exist on disk with matching content (no hallucinated prior-round citations).

Confirmed store.mjs's applyPost/applyTake/applyDeliver/applyVerifyAndPay remain a genuinely pure, unchanged state-transition module (no fs/network imports), consistent with the Purity Boundary Map's 'existing, unchanged' classification.

Confirmed applyAndSave()'s re-read-fresh-then-mutate-then-save sequence inside the '_board' lock genuinely matches REQ-102/PROP-102a-c's described target behavior (read control flow directly, not a grep).

Confirmed all 5 test files named in REQ-103's edge case exist, and that skills/economy/gig/package.json declares viem/zod/@modelcontextprotocol-sdk with no node_modules present in the main tree -- REQ-103's 'npm install needed in a fresh checkout' claim is accurate.

blockingFindings.summary: REQ-201 requires a 'documented safe default value' for BOOTSTRAP_RESERVE_USDC when unset/invalid, but no such default value is documented anywhere in either spec file -- unlike the codebase's existing analogous COMPUTE_RESERVE_USDC (concretely defaulted to 5 in runtime/loop/context.mjs:39).
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: PROP-201c cannot be implemented or tested as an exact-value assertion without a spec-authorized number; Phase 3 would have to invent the safety-critical fallback threshold itself, violating spec_fidelity's 'concrete enough to be implemented unambiguously' bar.

blockingFindings.summary: REQ-201's all-risky-tag pathological edge case (and PROP-201e) requires 'designated always-available slot(s)' to survive filtering, but filterCatalog's own stated 4-input signature (balance, slot names, risk tags, threshold) has no mechanism to distinguish an 'always-available' slot from an ordinary risk-tagged one when literally every slot -- including report/cook -- is tagged risky.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: The requirement demands behavior the specified pure-function signature cannot produce; an unspecified 5th signal or hardcoded allowlist would have to be invented at Phase 3 with no spec authority for which slot names qualify.

blockingFindings.summary: The existing liquidityDirective steer explicitly tells a low-balance agent to 'CLOSE a profitable HL position' via the hl_trade slot -- REQ-201 would simultaneously remove hl_trade from the catalog at low balance, since hl_trade is REQ-201's own named example of a capital-risking slot.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: A real functional deadlock (an unclosable, possibly losing, leveraged position) is created by this increment and is nowhere addressed by any REQ or PROP; this is exactly the kind of missed cross-cutting edge case spec_fidelity review must catch before implementation.

blockingFindings.summary: The Purity Boundary Map and Tier-1 assignment for PROP-101a/b/d claim the lock-staleness predicate is pure and unit-testable 'without touching the filesystem or real wall-clock sleeps (fake nowMs/mtimeMs injected)'. Direct inspection of lib/lock.mjs and __tests__/lock.test.mjs shows no such isolated pure function exists -- staleness is checked inline inside the effectful acquire(), and the actual tests use real fs + real setTimeout wall-clock waits, which is Tier 2 by the document's own definitions.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: This is a direct, evidenced contradiction between the verification architecture's purity/tier claims and the real code structure they describe -- exactly the purity-boundary-vs-code-structure check this review was tasked to perform, and it fails.

blockingFindings.summary: PROP-203b instructs the Phase-3 adversary to expect 'only the already-existing you decide framing' in prompt.mjs, but the actual current prompt.mjs already contains forceful ranking/steering text ('your FIRST action this wake MUST be economy/gig', 'Prefer this over re-yielding surplus', 'Do this BEFORE hl_trade / yield / anything else').
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: A verification instruction that mischaracterizes the baseline it tells a fresh-context adversary to compare against is a genuine verification_tool_mismatch that can produce a false-negative PASS on REQ-203's own design principle.
